title: Surgical Batch & Cache Advisor with SLO-aware Throttle Controls
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: We need a safe, automated way to apply batching and KV-prefix caching recommendations that reduces per-token cost while hard-guarding latency and throughput SLOs. Previous optimizers made aggressive profile changes that occasionally regressed p95 latency or reduced sustained throughput for bursty routes. Goal: Build a lightweight advisor that proposes per-route batch/cache profiles, a staged apply mechanism with SLO-aware throttle limiters and observability probes, and an automatic rollback path when anomaly detectors indicate SLA risk. The system should be usable by hosted and Dedicated customers and integrate with rollouts in the Console for visibility.
acceptance_criteria: Advisor generates per-route batching+cache suggestions based on 7 days of traffic and model sequence-length histograms
Safe-apply runbook: a canary apply to 2% traffic for 15 minutes followed by staged ramp to target, with automatic pause if SLOs break
SLO-aware throttle layer enforces hard caps on added queueing latency and token-rate changes per route
Anomaly detector flags regressions using p50/p95/p99 latency deltas and throughput shift; false positive rate < 3% on historical replay
Rollback automation reverts to previous config and emits a runbook ticket + link to first-failed probe traces and cost delta report
End-to-end integration tests and a demo in Console showing before/after cost and latency impact for a sample service
tasks: Data ingestion: export per-route token length distribution and latency/throughput time series (7d)
Advisor model: heuristics service that scores candidate batch/cache profiles with cost vs SLO risk
Throttle implementation: runtime limiter hooks that can apply soft/hard caps during rollout windows
Anomaly detectors: implement baseline-aware detectors using median absolute deviation and exponentially weighted windows
Rollout controller: canary -> ramp -> finalize with automatic rollback and manual-confirm path
Console UI: proposal card, staged rollout controls, and post-run analytics link to traces and cost savings

notes: Design trade-offs considered: conservative TTLs vs cache priming; chosen to prefer shorter TTL with prefetch hints for high-confidence prefixes
Anomaly detection approach: combine percentile delta checks with a token-rate shift detector to avoid misattributing load spikes to config changes
Rollback strategy: immediate revert on hard SLO breach; if soft warnings accumulate, pause ramp and open human review ticket
Operational runbook pointers: link to incident responder on-call, and to cost dashboard with per-route cost breakdown
